# Channel Clustering (CCM) vs. plain

- Family `voip`, L48/O12, L24/O6; every dataset with cluster runs
- k swept: 1, 2, 3, 6 (k = C is one cluster per channel)
- Models: EMForecaster (2025), DLinear (2023), TSMixer (2023), PatchTST (2023), Transformer (2017), LSTM (1997); ARIMA and Persistence are n/a (per-band by construction: one model per band, no gradient path to cluster)
- Values: the fixed train-mean membership protocol (`sl_test_fixed/*`), mean over seeds ± their sample standard deviation; (n=…) marks a cell with fewer seeds than the family's
- Val k: the k with the lowest seed-mean `sl_val_fixed/loss`, ranked over the k values that have every seed of the sweep (paradigms.choose_k, the same choice as the Paradigm Comparison); its cell is <u>underlined</u> once the choice is final, every k of the sweep with every seed of the family. Until then nothing is underlined and Val k says what the choice was ranked over
- Oracle k: the k with the lowest test value. It is chosen on the test split, so it is an upper bound, reported only to show how far validation lands from it; nothing here is selected on it
- Δ: the val-k cell against k = 1 and against plain, **bold** when better beyond the pooled seed standard deviation, ≈ inside it, unmarked when a side is incomplete

$k$ = 1 is one cluster over all channels: the plain network plus the cluster assigner, whose output cannot change a one-cluster forecast. It reproduces the plain cell within seed noise, not bit for bit: the assigner and the similarity loss draw from the global random stream, which changes every random draw training makes after them, the backbone's dropout masks among them. Largest per-seed relative MSE gap between $k$ = 1 and plain (logged numbers): EMForecaster (2025) 1.3e-02, DLinear (2023) 1.3e-03, TSMixer (2023) 7.4e-03, PatchTST (2023) 1.7e-02, Transformer (2017) 5.5e-03, LSTM (1997) 4.9e-03. Every multivariate and cluster run here trained eager, so none of it is a compile difference.
